Real ballot, researched with this tool on October 6, 2026 using a public building's address. AI research can be wrong: open the sources. This is not an endorsement. Get dates and places from your official election office (Franklin County Board of Elections).

The tool is neutral by default; the profile table shows how values match works.

Method

Each choice is shown side by side, with no scores. Records (what candidates did) come first, then questionnaire answers, then other statements, then donors and endorsements. Every line shows its kind, topic, date and source. After each comparison, a table shows how six example values profiles would score it from the same evidence; those scores are illustrations, not recommendations.

5 of 25 ballot items were researched for this sample.

Governor and Lieutenant Governor (Ohio)

Three tickets are printed on the ballot: Amy Acton and David Pepper, Don Kissick and James L. Mills, and Vivek Ramaswamy and Robert A. McColley.

Amy Acton (Democratic), running with David Pepper

  • [Public health] RECORD, 2020-06-11: As Ohio Department of Health director she issued or recommended the state's early COVID-19 orders (fitness-festival spectator ban March 4, 2020; statewide school closure within a week; cancellation of in-person voting on the March 17, 2020 primary day). She left the post June 11, 2020 and stayed on as an adviser to Gov. DeWine. Orders drew lawsuits and a House effort to limit her authority (AP via News4JAX). (source: www.news4jax.com)
  • [Taxes] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign page (viewed 2026-10-06, undated) proposes an Ohio earned income credit and a child tax credit of $1,000 per child ages 0-6 and $500 ages 7-18 for families earning up to $85,000; the page cites about 775,000 families and 1.4 million children. (source: actonforgovernor.com)
  • [Education] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign page (viewed 2026-10-06, undated) proposes restoring public school funding to a constitutional level and implementing the Fair School Funding Plan, redirecting voucher money to public schools with more accountability, and free school breakfast and lunch. (source: actonforgovernor.com)
  • [Health care] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign page (viewed 2026-10-06, undated) proposes a state 'Ohio Rx' drug-purchasing platform using Medicaid purchasing power, counting out-of-pocket drug costs toward deductibles, and state purchase of medical debt for relief. (source: actonforgovernor.com)
  • [Campaign finance] FUNDER, 2026-06-19: Signal Ohio (June 19, 2026), reporting the filing for April 16 to June 12, 2026: Acton raised $10.6 million in 2026 and held $8.1 million cash on hand. Secondhand; official Ohio SOS filing not opened. (source: signalcleveland.org)

Don Kissick (Libertarian), running with James L. Mills

  • [Taxes] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign page (viewed 2026-10-06, undated) supports ending property taxes in favor of 'local consumption based funding' and eliminating corporate subsidies to balance budgets. (source: donkissick.com)
  • [Government ethics] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign page proposes a five-year ban on legislators becoming lobbyists after leaving office, ending corporate contributions from regulated industries, and public searchable databases of government contracts. (source: donkissick.com)
  • [Energy and land use] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign page opposes data-center development on farmland and seeks to end special tax incentives for data centers. (source: donkissick.com)
  • [Civil liberties] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign page opposes automated license-plate camera networks and vehicle-tracking databases and calls for limits on mass-surveillance systems. (source: donkissick.com)

Vivek Ramaswamy (Republican), running with Robert A. McColley

  • [Federal service] RECORD, 2025-01-20: Named in November 2024 with Elon Musk to lead the advisory Department of Government Efficiency; left in January 2025 after saying he planned to run for governor (reported by WSET/ABC News). He has not held elected office. No state record to cite. (source: wset.com)
  • [Taxes] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign plan page (viewed 2026-10-06, undated): 'slash property taxes immediately,' eliminate capital gains taxes, phase out the state income tax, and gas-tax relief; data-center tax revenue to fund homeowner rebates. (source: vivekforohio.com)
  • [Education] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign plan page proposes literacy (3rd grade), numeracy (8th grade) and civics (12th grade) standards, more parent choice over where children learn, higher pay for top-performing teachers, and expanded career-technical programs. (source: vivekforohio.com)
  • [Public safety] STATED, 2026-10-06: Campaign plan page proposes stricter bail and sentencing for repeat violent offenders, support for local law enforcement capacity, and addressing severe psychiatric illness to redirect police resources. (source: vivekforohio.com)
  • [Campaign finance] FUNDER, 2026-06-19: Signal Ohio (June 19, 2026), reporting the filing for April 16 to June 12, 2026: Ramaswamy raised $9.6 million in 2026 and held $26.8 million cash on hand, including a $25 million personal loan made in 2025. Secondhand; official Ohio SOS filing not opened. (source: signalcleveland.org)

What to check: Which ticket's stated plans on taxes, schools, public safety and government a voter prefers, and how much weight to give each background: Acton's pandemic-era health agency record, Ramaswamy's business and short federal advisory role, and Kissick's campaign platform (no record or finance data found); no candidate has held elected office.

State Issue 3: Require voters to present photo identification

A General Assembly-initiated constitutional amendment that writes a photo ID requirement for voting into the Ohio Constitution.

What YES does:

  • Adds Section 5 to Article V: in-person voters must show an unexpired Ohio driver's license or state ID, U.S. passport or card, or military, Ohio National Guard or VA ID; the law may offer an alternative for a sincere religious objection; other voting methods need photo ID or, if law allows, a signature plus another unique identifier; effective immediately. Source: https://search-prod.lis.state.oh.us/api/v2/general_assembly_136/legislation/sjr10/05_EN/pdf/

What NO means: Photo ID stays a state statute (H.B. 458, signed January 6, 2023, in effect April 6, 2023), which the General Assembly can change by law. Source: https://ballotpedia.org/Ohio_Require_Voter_Identification_Amendment_(2026)

Cost estimate: No official fiscal estimate found (the Secretary of State's Issue 3 report returned HTTP 403). The Ohio Controlling Board approved the Secretary of State's request for county newspaper notices of the amendment and arguments (more than $300,000, per WKBN; the request was $388,002): https://www.wkbn.com/news/elections/ohio-approves-money-to-educate-on-voter-id-amendment-2/amp/

Strongest argument for YES: House Speaker Matt Huffman says photo ID is overwhelmingly popular and routine for ordinary transactions; Rep. Adam Bird says it gives voters a chance to protect free and fair elections (Ballotpedia). (ballotpedia.org)

Strongest argument for NO: Minority Leader Dani Isaacsohn says the ID rule is already law and the amendment will not change anyone's life; ACLU of Ohio's Gary Daniels says voter fraud is extremely rare and voting keeps getting harder (Ballotpedia). (ballotpedia.org)

  • [Elections] RECORD, 2026-06-10: Full text of Sub. S.J.R. 10 as sent to voters: new Article V, Section 5 (A) in-person photo ID, (B) other methods need photo ID or a signature plus unique identifier if authorized, (C) defines photo ID and unique identifier; effective on approval. (source: search-prod.lis.state.oh.us)
  • [Elections] RECORD, 2026-06-10: Senate adopted S.J.R. 10 22-9 on 6-3-2026 and the House adopted it 62-30 on 6-10-2026 (Ohio Legislature vote page); the resolution needed three-fifths of each chamber. (source: www.legislature.ohio.gov)
  • [Elections] RECORD, 2026: Ohio Controlling Board approved the Secretary of State's request (more than $300,000, per WKBN) as an emergency expense for county newspaper notices of the amendment and arguments; Sen. Catherine Ingram questioned whether newspapers reach underserved voters. (source: www.wkbn.com)
  • [Elections] STATED, 2026-10-06: Supporters listed by Ballotpedia include President Trump, Sens. Gavarone, McColley, Timken, Reps. Bird and Huffman, and gubernatorial candidates Acton and Ramaswamy; opponents include Sens. Blackshear and Smith, Reps. Isaacsohn, Russo and Sims, gubernatorial candidate Kissick, ACLU of Ohio and Common Cause Ohio. (source: ballotpedia.org)
  • [Campaign finance] FUNDER, 2026-10-06: As of October 2026 Ballotpedia had not identified ballot-measure committees registered to support or oppose the amendment; it shows $0 reported on both sides. (source: ballotpedia.org)

What to check: Whether placing an existing statutory ID requirement in the Constitution (harder to change later) is worth it, and whether the ID types and the mail-voting rule it specifies are the right ones.

Columbus Issues 8 and 9: charter amendments on how City Council is elected

Two proposed Columbus charter amendments would both limit council voting to residents of each district; Issue 9 also adds four at-large seats over two cycles.

What YES does:

  • Issue 8 (petition): only electors living in a district vote for or recall that district's council member; council stays at nine seats; ballots show citywide races plus the district race. Issue 9 (Council): the same district-only voting, plus two at-large seats elected in 2027 (seated 2028) and two more elected in 2029 (seated 2030), council growing from 9 to 11 to 13, a district map redraw in 2027 with allowed population variance rising from 1% to 7.5%, one-year district residency, and higher vote thresholds for some council actions. Sources: https://vote.franklincountyohio.gov/getmedia/a7a2dd78-e53f-4e74-933a-0ba0de9aaa4c/8-Full-OCOS-Charter-Amendment and https://vote.franklincountyohio.gov/getmedia/a3d9d75e-83ff-492a-98c4-a8cc09e1cd60/Notice-of-Election-Columbus-Charter-Amendment-2-Council

What NO means: Council members continue to be elected citywide while living in one of nine districts (WOSU describes the current system as candidates who live in a district but must win a citywide majority). Source: https://www.wosu.org/politics-government/2026-03-04/columbus-voters-may-see-dueling-ballot-issues-to-change-the-city-councils-hybrid-district-system

Cost estimate: No official cost estimate for either amendment was found; the 8/24/2026 ordinance and fiscal documents were not opened. Cost of added council seats UNVERIFIED.

Strongest argument for YES: Our City, Our Say's Will Petrick says changing how council is elected will bring more responsiveness and accountability; Council President Shannon Hardin says a growing city needs to give more people a seat at the table (ABC6). (abc6onyourside.com)

Strongest argument for NO: No organized opposition to the measures as printed was found. About the earlier petition drive only (WOSU, March 2026, before either measure was final): Jonathan Beard, who backed a separate district-only proposal with a new map, said the petition version ignored Black Columbus interests. (www.wosu.org)

  • [Local elections] RECORD, 2026-08-24: Columbus City Council voted 8-0 on August 24, 2026 to place the petition amendment (Issue 8) on the November ballot and 8-0 to place its own amendment (Issue 9), per ABC6. (source: abc6onyourside.com)
  • [Local elections] RECORD, 2026-10-06: Issue 8 full text (Franklin County BOE): amends Charter Secs. 3, 4, 5 and 46 so council members are elected and recalled only by electors of their own district. (source: vote.franklincountyohio.gov)
  • [Local elections] RECORD, 2026-09-14: Issue 9 notice of election (Franklin County BOE, dated 9/14/2026): adds at-large seats, redraws map in 2027, 150-signature district and 250-signature at-large petition thresholds, 15% recall threshold by district or citywide. (source: vote.franklincountyohio.gov)
  • [Local elections] STATED, 2026-08-24: WOSU (8/24/2026) reports Council President Shannon Hardin and Council member Rob Dorans said they would support both amendments in November; Dorans said the two ideas complement one another. (source: wosu.org)
  • [Local elections] STATED, 2026-03-04: Kwesi Low (Columbus Stand Up) argued district-only voting would give districts leaders attentive to their challenges and cut campaign costs; Jonathan Beard criticized the petition drive's version (March 2026, before the final measures) as ignoring Black Columbus interests. (source: www.wosu.org)
  • [Campaign finance] FUNDER, 2026-10-06: No campaign-finance totals for committees supporting or opposing Issue 8 or 9 were found in the sources opened. (source: www.wosu.org)

What to check: Whether a voter wants district-only voting on the existing nine seats (Issue 8), a larger 13-member council with four at-large seats and a new map (Issue 9), or one of them only; how the two interact if both pass is unresolved in the sources found.

Open items

  • DISTRICTS: Ohio Secretary of State pages and district PDFs returned HTTP 403 to every fetch, so no official SOS lookup was opened. Districts (Congress 15, Ohio Senate 15, Ohio House 1) come from the U.S. Census Bureau geocoder run on the Statehouse's public coordinates (https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/geographies/coordinates?x=-83.0003&y=39.9611&benchmark=Public_AR_Current&vintage=Current_Current&layers=all&format=json). The Ohio House 1 result is consistent with Rep. Jarrells' official House page (District 1, Columbus) but that page does not prove the building's district. Congressional District 15 is UNVERIFIED by an Ohio-source map: nearby points return District 3 and District 15, so the building sits in a boundary area. Confirm with the Franklin County sample ballot generator at https://vote.franklincountyohio.gov.
  • Columbus voters in some precincts also get precinct-level liquor local-option questions (#10A through #17b on the certified list). Whether any applies to the Statehouse precinct is UNVERIFIED; the certified questions list was revised 9/4/2026 (pages marked 9/1 and 9/4), after which the Board may revise it again.
  • Judicial pairings: the Common Pleas General and Domestic Relations, and Court of Appeals seats are listed above as separate UNCONTESTED seats because each candidate has a different term-commencing date on the Franklin County list. No second source (campaign page or court roster) was found for these pairings. The Probate seat (Green, Junga, same date) is corroborated by Columbus Bar Association profiles for both.
  • Write-in column: the PDF header is garbled ('DWrite-In'). Candidates with party 'N/A' and 'Yes' in that column are treated as declared write-ins. Gary Josephson (U.S. House 15) and Greg Levy (U.S. Senate, 'Other-party c') show no such flag and are listed as printed candidates; this reading is UNVERIFIED.
  • Whether Issue 8 or Issue 9 prevails if both pass: one news outlet (Axios, not opened, search snippet only) says the charter gives the win to the issue with more votes; the 8/24/2026 council ordinance text was not opened. UNVERIFIED.
  • Ohio House 1 incumbent's press release on a 'Gas Tax Holiday Act' (HB 1019, House vote 78-16) could not be matched: the legislature.ohio.gov HB 1019 page shows no votes recorded. Left out of evidence.
  • Campaign finance for Governor is secondhand (Signal Ohio and NBC4 reports of official filings); the Ohio Secretary of State finance site was blocked (HTTP 403).
  • Passage threshold and turnout conditions for Issue 3 and Issues 8/9 were not checked in an official source.
  • Probate Court: Kelly Green's current title (Chief Magistrate) is supported by her Columbus Bar Association profile only; the court's staff page (probate.franklincountyohio.gov) returned HTTP 403. UNVERIFIED by the court.
  • Ohio Secretary of State pages (candidate lists, Issue 3 Ballot Board report with official YES/NO arguments, campaign finance site, district maps) blocked automated access with HTTP 403; official YES/NO arguments and fiscal analysis for Issue 3 could not be read.
  • Campaign finance: no state-level filings opened for Governor, House 1 or Probate; Governor totals are news reports of the filings.
  • Kissick: no record, no finance data, and no second source beyond his campaign site found.
  • Greff: no legislative or office record; only aggregator and campaign-homepage statements.
  • Green and Junga: experience claims rest on Columbus Bar Association profiles supplied by the candidates, including Green's current title (the probate court's page returned HTTP 403); no bar ratings, reversals or conduct findings were checked.
  • Columbus Issues 8 and 9: no official fiscal estimate, no committee funding, and no confirmation of the conflict rule if both pass.
  • Other statewide offices and Congress, Senate and Supreme Court races are listed but not researched (scope limit of 5 items).
